text:
omar (PM): Quick sync — need to lock SLOs and rollout acceptance for the embeddings endpoint this week. Customer ask: sub-50ms median for small vectors, and reasonable p95 under peak for paid tiers. Thoughts?

nina (Eng): We should separate targets by tier. Free tier: best-effort p95, paid: p95 <= 120ms, p50 <= 50ms sounds reasonable given current infra.

jeff (SRE): Agree on tiering. Also need explicit error budget and a degradation policy. If p95 blows past target for 15m, trigger telemetry alert and route to fallback.

kai (ML): Fallback options: 1) lower-precision quantized variant (faster but minor quality delta), 2) reduced batched size with aggressive early-exit, 3) route to regional cheaper pool. We should define acceptable quality regression thresholds.

omar (PM): Good list. Proposal: paid tier SLOs: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 120ms, error rate < 1% (5xx + 4xx client retries). Error budget monthly: 99.5% availability. Degrade plan: prefer quantized variant, else fallback region, else serve cached vectors with notice.

elaine (PM): For acceptance: PRD test harness that runs 30m synthetic load, verifies p95 and error rate under 1.2x projected QPS. Also require no more than 10% quality drop measured by our embedding-similarity eval set when using quantized fallback.

nina (Eng): Implementation notes: need a circuit breaker in router with weighted fallback. Router config example:
```
route {
  primary: model-v2
  fallback: [model-v2-quant, model-v1-regional]
  rules: {
    p95_over: 120ms -> activate fallback
    error_rate_over: 1% -> activate fallback
  }
}
```
Router must emit metrics: route.choice, route.latency_ms, route.quality_delta.

jeff (SRE): Add runbook steps in case of sustained p95 breach: 1) confirm metric (p95 sustained > threshold for 15m), 2) check infra (GPU utilization, queue depth), 3) flip fallback policy to quantized, 4) notify customers if >1h. Also add automated rollback to primary after 10m stable under threshold.

kai (ML): Edge case: some customers are sensitive to embedding drift. We should allow per-customer opt-out of quantized fallback and mark them as "no-degrade" in config. That will lower their availability guarantees but keep correctness. Need billing/legal signoff for SLA differences.

omar (PM): Good call. Acceptance criteria summary to include in PRD (for sign-off):
- Paid SLOs: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 120ms, error rate <1%
- Integration tests: 30m load at 1.2x expected QPS passing SLOs with primary and with quantized fallback enabled
- Quality threshold: quantized model similarity >= 90% vs primary on eval set
- Runbook + automated fallback implementation present in console
- Per-customer opt-out flag and billing/SLA note

elaine (PM): Who owns QA for the quality threshold? Need clear owner and dataset.

kai (ML): I'll own the eval set and run the similarity checks. Will post dataset link and baseline numbers by EOD.

jeff (SRE): I'll draft the runbook + alert conditions. Want to include a dashboard tile for per-route error budget burn and a golden signal.

omar (PM): Ok action items: kai -> eval set + baseline, jeff -> runbook + alerting, nina -> router + metrics, elaine -> update PRD acceptance section and coordinate SLA wording. I'll assemble the PRD PR and tag reviewers.

slo-bot: Note: creating a follow-up RFC thread for "Embeddings SLO + graceful degradation". Link will be posted when available. :spiral_calendar_pad: 

omar (PM): Thanks — let's land the RFC + PRD by Friday so we can start canary early next week.

nina (Eng): +1. I'll prototype router config in staging and share results tomorrow.

kai (ML): Baselines posted: similarity=0.93 for quantized vs primary on small-vectors set. Upload link: https://internal.redwood/ml/emb-quant-baselines

elaine (PM): Great. I'll draft the acceptance checklist and include the billing opt-out language.

jeff (SRE): Draft runbook in #incidents and will link from RFC.

omar (PM): Perfect — thanks team. If anyone spots an edge-case not covered (long-tail payload sizes, regional cold starts), drop it here and I'll fold into the PRD.
